successors.name: Safavid dynasty
successors.text: Azerbaijan (July 1501), Iraq-i Ajam, Fars and Kerman (summer 1503), Diyar Bakr (1507-08) and Mesopotamia with Baghdad (autumn 1508)

ledger.x: 1378: Qara Yuluk Uthman Beg founds the Aq Qoyunlu confederation.
1402: Timur grants Diyar Bakr to Kara Yuluk Osman ('Timur granted them Diyar Bakr in 1402'); Mardin is part of the Diyarbakır governorship.
1403: Âmid (Diyarbakır) becomes the capital and the Aq Qoyunlu become sultans (infobox 'Âmid (1403-1468)').
Page silent: Cliopatria's 1415 shape adds about 20,000 km2 in Raqqa and Hasakah (Syria) to the Diyar Bakr core; no page opened dates or explains it.
1465: Uzun Hasan captures Harput (listed under his war with Dulkadir: 'he captured Harput in 1465').
30 October (or 11 November) 1467: Uzun Hasan defeats and kills Jahan Shah at the Battle of Chapakchur, near Bingol.
1468: the Qara Qoyunlu collapse ('the collapse of the Qara Qoyunlu control in the Middle East'; Hasan Ali's brief reign 1467-68).
1468: 'Aq Qoyunlu defeated the Qara Qoyunlu and took Iraq, Azerbaijan and western Iran'.
1468: the plateau Jahan Shah took in 1447-1453 passes to Uzun Hasan with the end of the Qara Qoyunlu.
1468: the seat moves from Âmid to Tabriz (infobox 'Tabriz (1468 - 6 January 1478)').
July 1470: Uzun Hasan temporarily captures Herat from Sultan Husayn Bayqara ('Herat temporarily captured from Sultan Husayn Bayqara (Khorasan)').
1470: the capture of Herat is only 'temporary'; the page gives no date for the withdrawal.

Page silent on who held these lands and when the Aq Qoyunlu took them: the step from the corrected 1468 shape to Cliopatria's 1475 shape adds about 1,070 cells (270,000 km2) here, to within 30 cells of fringe, none of them in a Qara Qoyunlu shape of the dossier set.
Page silent on the year: the lead says Hormuz 'recognized Aq Qoyunlu suzerainty'; placed where Cliopatria's shape reaches the Gulf coast.

July 1501: Ismail occupies Tabriz after defeating the Aq Qoyunlu ruler Alvand at Sharur ('After occupying Tabriz, Ismail took the title Padshah-i Iran'); the Aq Qoyunlu page dates the Iranian collapse to autumn 1501.
Summer 1503: 'Iraq-Ajami, Fars, and Kerman conquered' by Ismail.
Page silent: Hormuz's recognition of Aq Qoyunlu suzerainty lapses with the loss of Fars and Kerman in 1503; no page says so.
1507-1508: Diyarbakir passes to the Safavids.
Autumn 1508: Ismail and Husayn Beg Shamlu seize Baghdad and Mesopotamia.
1508: the Aq Qoyunlu end ('putting an end to the Aq Qoyunlu', Baghdad seized 1508); the Aq Qoyunlu page: collapse in Iran 1503, end in Mesopotamia 1508.

wars.name: Uzun Hasan's war with Dulkadir over Harput
Qara Qoyunlu-Aq Qoyunlu war
wars.outcome: Jahan Shah's 1466 advance reaches Mush and withdraws; Uzun Hasan wins at Chapakchur (30 October or 11 November 1467) and takes Iraq, Azerbaijan and western Iran by 1468.

wars.name: Battle of Qarabagh (Aq Qoyunlu-Timurid war)
wars.outcome: Abu Sa'id Mirza is defeated at the Battle of Qarabagh in 1469 and executed; no frontier changes.

wars.name: Aq Qoyunlu capture of Herat
wars.outcome: Herat temporarily captured from Sultan Husayn Bayqara in July 1470.

wars.name: Ottoman-Aq Qoyunlu war
wars.outcome: Uzun Hasan advances to Akşehir and pillages Tokat in 1471, fights at Tercan and is defeated at Otlukbeli in late summer 1473 by Mehmed II; the pages record no border change.

wars.name: Aq Qoyunlu succession wars
wars.outcome: Khalil (a few months in 1478), Ya'qub (1478-1490), Rustam, Baysungur (dethroned 1491, killed 1493) and Ahmad Bey (died December 1497) fight for the throne; the realm divides among rival rulers (Alvand, Qasim, Mohammad, Murad) after Ahmad's death.

wars.name: Safavid conquest of the Aq Qoyunlu
wars.outcome: Ismail wins at Sharur (1501), occupies Tabriz (July 1501), defeats an Aq Qoyunlu army in 1502, takes Iraq-i Ajam and Fars after Hamadan and Kerman (summer 1503), Diyarbakir (1507-08) and Baghdad (1508).

certainty.note: A Turkoman confederation of pastures and governorships; no treaty or survey frontier appears on any page.
